content.text: {"utterance": "Sam, you say a learner who can defend a step will say where the notes fail and why, and that luck gives no such location. But take the revealed cook: she adapts the recipe with her notebook and a friend, yet cannot recite it. Suppose she catches the wrong stock quantity only because her friend says \"that looks high.\" Has she learned, or has the friend? Tell me, all of you: what would you observe to separate competent use of help from dependence?", "cites": ["SO2"], "memory": "Pressed Sam: error-catching may be borrowed from the friend. Live question: what observation separates competent use of notebook and friend from dependence, and does assistance change what was learned or undermine the claim?"}
